sanskrit: ud vāṁ cakṣur varuṇa supratīkaṁ devoyor eti sūryas tatanvān | abhi yo viśvā bhuvanāni caṣṭe sa manyum martyeṣv ā ciketa ||
english: Up goes the eye of Varuṇa, bright-faced and all-pervading — the Sun, spreading wide, who surveys all beings; he perceives the wrath that is among mortals.

sanskrit: pra vāṁ sa mitrāvaruṇāv ṛtāvā vipro manmāni dīrghaśrud iyarti | yasya brahmāṇi sukratū avātha ā yat kratvā na śaradaḥ pṛṇaithe ||
english: For you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, that wise and far-famed one of true order sends forth his hymns; you two, of excellent power, have supported his prayers — as with creative force you fulfil the years.

sanskrit: proror mitrāvaruṇā pṛthivyāḥ pra diva ṛṣvād bṛhataḥ sudānū | spaśo dadhāthe oṣadhīṣu vikṣv ṛdhag yato animiṣaṁ rakṣamāṇā ||
english: From the wide earth and from the lofty and vast heaven, O Mitra-Varuṇa of liberal gifts, you have set your spies among the plants and peoples — watching unblinking from the place whence they arose.

sanskrit: śaṁsā mitrasya varuṇasya dhāma śuṣmo rodasī badbadhe mahitvā | ayan māsā ayajvanām avīrāḥ pra yajñamanmā vṛjanaṁ tirāte ||
english: Declare the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa — their might has filled both worlds with its greatness. The months of those who offer no sacrifice pass without heroic issue; but the one whose thought is sacrifice carries his community through.

sanskrit: amūrā viśvā vṛṣaṇāv imā vāṁ na yāsu citraṁ dadṛśe na yakṣam | druhaḥ sacante anṛtā janānāṁ na vāṁ niṇyāny acite abhūvan ||
english: All these worlds, O mighty bulls, are your domain; in them no wondrous portent or goblin is unseen. The wicked among men who follow deception — your secret works have not gone unobserved by you.

sanskrit: sam u vāṁ yajñam mahayaṁ namobhir huve vām mitrāvaruṇā sabādhaḥ | pra vāṁ manmāny ṛcase navāni kṛtāni brahma jujuṣann imāni ||
english: I magnify your rite and call upon you both, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with reverences and earnest petition; may these new hymns, composed for the poem, delight you — prayers fashioned and offered to you.

sanskrit: iyaṁ deva purohitir yuvabhyāṁ yajñeṣu mitrāvaruṇāv akāri | viśvāni durgā pipṛtaṁ tiro no yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: This priestly service, O Mitra-Varuṇa, has been rendered to you both at the sacrifices. Carry us through all difficulties; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: ut sūryo bṛhad arcīṁṣy aśret puru viśvā janima mānu ṣāṇām | samo divā dadṛśe rocamānaḥ kratvā kṛtaḥ sukṛtaḥ kartṛbhir bhūt ||
english: The Sun has risen on high, ascending with his broad blazing rays over all the manifold origins of humankind; shining equally across the sky he is seen — fashioned by wisdom, made excellent by his makers.

sanskrit: sa sūrya prati puro na ud gā ebhiḥ stomebhir etaśebhir evaiḥ | pra no mitrāya varuṇāya voco 'nāgaso aryamṇe agnaye ca ||
english: Rise, O Sūrya, before our dwellings as before, with these hymns, with these swift steeds as your paths; speak forth our guiltlessness to Mitra and Varuṇa, to Aryaman and to Agni.

sanskrit: vi naḥ sahasraṁ śurudho radantv ṛtāvāno varuṇo mitro agniḥ | yacchantu candrā upamaṁ no arkam ā naḥ kāmaṁ pūpurantu stavānāḥ ||
english: May Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni — keepers of holy order — open to us a thousand refreshing streams; may the gleaming ones bestow on us the highest gift of praise, and may they, when glorified, satisfy our desire.

sanskrit: dyāvābhūmī adite trāsīthāṁ no ye vāṁ jajñuḥ sujanimāna ṛṣve | mā heḻe bhūma varuṇasya vāyor mā mitrasya priyatamasya nṛṇām ||
english: O Heaven-and-Earth, O Aditi, protect us — you to whom those of beautiful birth have been born, high and great ones; may we not incur the wrath of Varuṇa or Vāyu, nor of Mitra who is most dear to men.

sanskrit: pra bāhavā sisṛtaṁ jīvase na ā no gavyūtim ukṣataṁ ghṛtena | ā no jane śravayataṁ yuvānā śrutam me mitrāvaruṇā havemā ||
english: Stretch out your arms for our life; sprinkle our pasture-land with ghee. Make us heard among our people, O you two youths — hear our call, O Mitra-Varuṇa, as I invoke you.

sanskrit: nū mitro varuṇo aryamā nas tmane tokāya varivo dadhantu | sugā no viśvā supathāni santu yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant us wide scope for ourselves and our offspring; may all paths be easy-going for us; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: ud v eti subhago viśvacakṣāḥ sādhāraṇaḥ sūryo mānu ṣāṇām | cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasya devaś carmeva yaḥ samavivyak tamāṁsi ||
english: Up rises the bountiful, all-seeing Sun, common to all mankind; the divine eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, who has spread away the darkness as if it were a skin.

sanskrit: ud v eti prasavītā janānāṁ mahān ketur arṇavaḥ sūryasya | samānaṁ cakram paryāvivṛtsan yad etaśo vahati dhūrṣu yuktaḥ ||
english: Up rises the great impeller of people, the mighty banner, the flood of the Sun — seeking to set the common wheel in motion, when the bay steed is yoked and draws at the pole.

sanskrit: vibhrājamāna uṣasām upasthād rebhair ud ety anumadhyamānaḥ | eṣa me devaḥ savitā cacchanda yaḥ samānaṁ na praminātī dhāma ||
english: Blazing forth from the lap of the Dawns, he rises, praised by the singers; this god Savitṛ has pleased me — he who does not diminish the common ordinance.

sanskrit: divo rukma urucakṣā ud eti dūrearthas taraṇir bhrājamānaḥ | nūnaṁ janāḥ sūryeṇa prasūtā ayann arthāni kṛṇavann apāṁsi ||
english: The golden ornament of heaven, the far-sighted, the swift, the brilliant, rises with his goal afar; now, driven forth by the Sun, men set out on their journeys and accomplish their tasks.

sanskrit: yatrā cakrur amṛtā gātum asmai śyeno na dīyann anv eti pāthaḥ | prati vāṁ sūra uditē vidhema namobhir mitrāvaruṇota havyaiḥ ||
english: Where the immortals have fashioned his way — he follows the path like a falcon swooping down; at the rising of the Sun we honor you two, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with reverences and oblations.

sanskrit: nū mitro varuṇo aryamā nas tmane tokāya varivo dadhantu | sugā no viśvā supathāni santu yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant us wide scope for ourselves and our offspring; may all paths be easy-going for us; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: divi kṣayantā rajasaḥ pṛthivyām pra vāṁ ghṛtasya nirṇijo dadīran | havyaṁ no mitro aryamā sujāto rājā sukṣatro varuṇo juṣanta ||
english: Dwelling in heaven above the realm of earth, may the streaming libations of ghee be offered to you both. May Mitra and Aryaman of noble birth, the good king, the good ruler Varuṇa, delight in our oblation.

sanskrit: ā rājānā maha ṛtasya gopā sindhupatī kṣatriyā yātam arvāk | iḻāṁ no mitrāvaruṇota vṛṣṭim ava diva invataṁ jīradānū ||
english: Come hither, you two kings, great guardians of holy order, lords of the rivers, rulers — come to us; O Mitra-Varuṇa of swift bestowal, send down to us refreshing food and rain from heaven.

sanskrit: mitras tan no varuṇo devo aryaḥ pra sādhisthebhiḥ pathibhir nayantu | bravad yathā na ād ariḥ sudāsa iṣā madema saha devagopāḥ ||
english: May Mitra, Varuṇa and the noble god Aryaman lead us forth by the safest paths; may none harm Sudās when he speaks — may we rejoice in nourishment, guarded by the gods.

sanskrit: yo vāṁ gartam manasā takṣad etam ūrdhvāṁ dhītiṁ kṛṇavad dhārayac ca | ukṣethāṁ mitrāvaruṇā ghṛtena tā rājānā sukṣitīs tarpayethām ||
english: He who fashions for you in his mind this seat of honor, who holds his thought upright and sustains it — drench him, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with ghee; you two kings, satisfy him with good dwellings.

sanskrit: eṣa stomo varuṇa mitra tubhyaṁ somaḥ śukro na vāyave 'yāmi | aviṣṭaṁ dhiyo jigṛtam puraṁdhīr yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: This praise, O Varuṇa, this hymn, is dedicated to you and Mitra, pure as soma for Vāyu; protect our thoughts, grasp our minds; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: prati vāṁ sūra uditē sūktair mitraṁ huve varuṇam pūtadakṣam | yayor asuryam akṣitaṁ jyeṣṭhaṁ viśvasya yāmann ācitā jigatnu ||
english: At the rising of the Sun I call upon Mitra and upon Varuṇa of pure might with well-spoken hymns — whose lordly power is imperishable and supreme, both perceived and advancing in the journey of all.

sanskrit: tā hi devānām asurā tāv aryā tā naḥ kṣitīḥ karatam ūrjayantīḥ | aśyāma mitrāvaruṇā vayaṁ vāṁ dyāvā ca yatra pīpayan ahā ca ||
english: For they are the lords of the gods, those two nobles; may they make our dwellings vigorous with strength. May we, O Mitra-Varuṇa, attain to you two — where heaven and the days nourish and delight.

sanskrit: tā bhūripāśāv anṛtasya setū daratyetū ripave martyāya | ṛtasya mitrāvaruṇā pathā vāṁ apo na nāvā duritā tarema ||
english: You two have many snares and are barriers of falsehood, hard to cross for the mortal enemy; along the path of holy order, O Mitra-Varuṇa, may we cross difficulties as if by boat across the waters.

sanskrit: ā no mitrāvaruṇā havyajuṣṭiṁ ghṛtair gavyūtim ukṣataṁ iḻābhiḥ | prati vāṁ atra varam ā janāya pṛṇītam udno divyasya cāroḥ ||
english: Come, O Mitra-Varuṇa, be pleased with our oblation; sprinkle our pasture-land with ghee and with refreshing food; bestow upon the people here the best of gifts; fill us with the fair waters of heaven.

sanskrit: eṣa stomo varuṇa mitra tubhyaṁ somaḥ śukro na vāyave 'yāmi | aviṣṭaṁ dhiyo jigṛtam puraṁdhīr yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: This praise, O Varuṇa, this hymn, is dedicated to you and Mitra, pure as soma for Vāyu; protect our thoughts, grasp our minds; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: pra mitrayoḥ varuṇayoḥ stomo na etu śūṣyaḥ | namasvān tuvijātayoḥ ||
english: Let our mighty praise go forth to Mitra and Varuṇa, full of reverence — to the two born of great strength.

sanskrit: yā dhārayanta devāḥ sudakṣā dakṣapitarā | asuryāya pramāhasā ||
english: Those two gods of excellent discernment, the fathers of discernment, uphold all with their lordly greatness.

sanskrit: tā naḥ stipā tanūpā varuṇa jaritṝṇām | mitra sādhayataṁ dhiyaḥ ||
english: You two who guard the body and protect the person of singers — O Varuṇa, O Mitra, further our thoughts.

sanskrit: yad adya sūra uditē 'nāgā mitro aryamā | suvāti savitā bhagaḥ ||
english: What blameless gift Mitra, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Bhaga send forth today at the rising of the Sun —

sanskrit: suprāvīr astu sa kṣayaḥ pra nu yāman sudānavaḥ | ye no aṁho 'ti piprati ||
english: May that abode be well-aided; may the liberal ones, in their course, carry us beyond the trouble — those who lead us past distress.

sanskrit: uta svarājo aditir adabdhasya vratasya ye | maho rājāna īśate ||
english: And the self-sovereign Aditi, along with those who govern the uninjurable ordinance — those great kings are lords.

sanskrit: prati vāṁ sūra uditē mitraṁ gṛṇīṣe varuṇam | aryamaṇaṁ riśādasam ||
english: At the rising of the Sun I praise Mitra and Varuṇa, and Aryaman the destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: rāyā hiraṇyayā matir iyam avṛkāya śavase | iyaṁ viprā medhasātaye ||
english: This thought is for the golden wealth and the inviolable might; this inspired prayer is for the winning of the sacred drink.

sanskrit: te syāma deva varuṇa te mitra sūribhiḥ saha | iṣaṁ svaś ca dhīmahi ||
english: May we be yours, O Varuṇa, yours, O Mitra, together with the generous patrons; may we hold fast nourishment and light.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ sūracakṣaso 'gnijihvā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | trīṇi ye yemur vidathāni dhītibhir viśvāni paribhūtibhiḥ ||
english: Many are they, the eye of the Sun, Agni-tongued, increasers of holy order, who have governed with their thoughts the three assemblies, encompassing all things.

sanskrit: vi ye dadhuḥ śaradam māsam ād ahar yajñam aktuṁ cād ṛcam | anāpyaṁ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṁ rājāna āśata ||
english: They who have established the year, the month, the day, the sacrifice, the night, and the sacred verse — Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman have attained to the sovereignty which none can approach; the kings have encompassed it.

sanskrit: tad vo adya manāmahe sūktaiḥ sūra uditē | yad ohate varuṇo mitro aryamā yūyam ṛtasya rathyaḥ ||
english: This we meditate upon for you today with well-spoken hymns at the rising of the Sun — that which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman bear together: you are the charioteers of holy order.

sanskrit: ṛtāvāna ṛtajātā ṛtāvṛdho ghorāso anṛtadviṣaḥ | teṣāṁ vaḥ sumne succhardiṣṭame naraḥ syāma ye ca sūrayaḥ ||
english: Keepers of holy order, born of holy order, increasers of holy order, awesome and haters of falsehood — in the most glorious shelter of your favor may we men and our patrons be.

sanskrit: ud u tyad darśataṁ vapur diva eti prativare | yad īm āśur vahati deva etaśo viśvasmai cakṣase aram ||
english: Up goes that beautiful form visible from afar on the back of heaven — when the divine swift steed Etaśa carries it onward, sufficient for the sight of all.

sanskrit: śīrṣṇaḥ-śīrṣṇo jagatas tasthūṣas patiṁ samayā viśvam ā rajaḥ | sapta svasāraḥ suvitāya sūryaṁ vahanti harito rathe ||
english: Lord of every moving and stationary being, pervading all the realm alike — the seven bay mares in the chariot carry the Sun for the good of all.

sanskrit: tac cakṣur devahitaṁ śukram uccarat | paśyema śaradaḥ śataṁ jīvema śaradaḥ śatam ||
english: That bright eye set in place by the gods rises high — may we see a hundred autumns; may we live a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: kāvyebhir adābhyā yātaṁ varuṇa dyumat | mitraś ca somapītaye ||
english: Come, O inviolable Varuṇa, and Mitra, splendidly, with your poetic powers, to drink the Soma.

sanskrit: divo dhāmabhir varuṇa mitraś cā yātam adruhā | pibataṁ somam ātujī ||
english: With the forms of heaven, O Varuṇa and Mitra, come — you who are without deceit; drink the Soma eagerly.

sanskrit: ā yātaṁ mitrāvaruṇā juṣāṇāv āhutiṁ narā | pātaṁ somam ṛtāvṛdhā ||
english: Come hither, O Mitra-Varuṇa, delighting in the oblation, O lords; drink the Soma, O increasers of holy order.

sanskrit: prati vāṁ rathaṁ nṛpatī jaradhyai haviṣmatā manasā yajñiyena | yo vāṁ dūto na dhiṣṇyāv ajīgar acchā sūnur na pitarā vivakmi ||
english: To praise your chariot, O lords of men, with a mind full of oblation and devoted to the sacrifice — as a son speaks to his two fathers, so I address you who are like an envoy arousing two high-minded ones.

sanskrit: aśocy agniḥ samidhāno asme upo adṛśran tamasaś cid antāḥ | aceti ketor uṣasaḥ purastāc chriye divo duhitur jāyamānaḥ ||
english: Agni has been kindled and blazes in our midst; even the borders of the darkness have become visible. The banner of Dawn in the east has been perceived — the daughter of heaven is being born in beauty.

sanskrit: abhi vāṁ nūnam aśvinā suhotā stomai siṣakti nāsatyā vivākvān | pūrvībhir yātam pathyābhir arvāk svarvidā vasumatā rathena ||
english: The skilled invoker now follows you two, O Aśvins, the speakers of truth, with hymns as he raises his voice. Come hither along the ancient paths with your light-winning, wealth-laden chariot.

sanskrit: avor vāṁ nūnam aśvinā yuvākur huve yad vāṁ sute mādhvī vasūyuḥ | ā vāṁ vahantu sthavirāso aśvāḥ pibātho asme suṣutā madhūni ||
english: Now with yearning I call you two, O Aśvins, for help, when, at the pressing of the Soma, one desirous of wealth calls to you two who are sweet. May your strong horses bring you; drink the sweet draughts pressed here for us.

sanskrit: prācīm u devāśvinā dhiyam me 'mṛdhrāṁ sātaye kṛtaṁ vasūyum | viśvā aviṣṭaṁ vāja ā puraṁdhīs tā naḥ śaktaṁ śacīpatī śacībhiḥ ||
english: Turn my eastward-directed, unfailing, wealth-seeking thought toward winning, O divine Aśvins. Help all the wise ones in the contest; grant us that, O lords of power, with your powers.

sanskrit: aviṣṭaṁ dhīṣv aśvinā na āsu prajāvad reto ahrayaṁ no astu | ā vāṁ toke tanaye tūtujānāḥ suratnāso devavītiṁ gamema ||
english: Help our thoughts, O Aśvins; may our seed among them be fruitful and shameless. Hastening to you in respect of our offspring and progeny, may we, rich in good gifts, come to the feast of the gods.

sanskrit: eṣa sya vāṁ pūrvagatveva sakhye nidhir hito mādhvī rāto asme | aheḻatā manasā yātam arvāg aśnantā havyam mānu ṣīṣu vikṣu ||
english: This treasure of sweetness, as in a former friendship, has been placed and given to us by you two. Come hither with a friendly mind and enjoy the oblation among the human peoples.

sanskrit: ekasmin yoge bhuraṇā samāne pari vāṁ sapta sravato ratho gāt | na vāyanti subhvo devayuktā ye vāṁ dhūrṣu taraṇayo vahanti ||
english: In one single draught, at the common yoke, your chariot goes around the seven streams; they do not tire, the vigorous ones yoked by the gods, those fleet ones who draw you at the pole.

sanskrit: asaścatā maghavadbhyo hi bhūtaṁ ye rāyā maghadeyaṁ junanti | pra ye bandhuṁ sūnṛtābhis tirante gavyā pṛñcanto aśvyā maghāni ||
english: Be inexhaustible to the generous ones who speed on with wealth to the gift of bounty, who press forward with true words to cross over kinship-obligations, mixing cattle-wealth with horse-wealth as their gifts.

sanskrit: nū me havam ā śṛṇutaṁ yuvānā yāsiṣṭaṁ vartir aśvināv irāvat | dhattaṁ ratnāni jarataṁ ca sūrīn yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Now hear my call, O two young ones; come, O Aśvins, on a path that brings refreshment. Bestow treasures and let the patrons grow old in honor; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: ā śubhrā yātam aśvinā svaśvā giro dasrā jujuṣāṇā yuvākoḥ | havyāni ca pratibhṛtā vītaṁ naḥ ||
english: Come with your bright, fair-horsed chariot, O wonder-working Aśvins, delighting in the hymns of one who longs for you; enjoy the oblations brought to you — come to us.

sanskrit: pra vāṁ andhāṁsi madyāny asthur araṁ gantaṁ haviṣo vītaye me | tiro aryo havanāni śrutaṁ naḥ ||
english: The intoxicating drinks have gone forth to you; come readily to enjoy my oblation; hear our invocations across the distance of the stranger's land.

sanskrit: pra vāṁ ratho manojavā iyarti tiro rajāṁsy aśvinā śatotiḥ | asmabhyaṁ sūryāvasū iyānaḥ ||
english: Your swift-as-thought chariot sets out, O Aśvins, bearing a hundred aids across the realms of space — moving toward us, O you who have the Sun for your treasure.

sanskrit: ayaṁ ha yad vāṁ devayā u adrir ūrdhvo vivakti somasud yuvabhyām | ā valgū vipro vavṛtīta havyaiḥ ||
english: When this pressing-stone, rising high, speaks for you the god-seekers, O Soma-presser, to you two — may the inspired singer turn to you with beautiful oblations.

sanskrit: citraṁ ha yad vāṁ bhojanaṁ nv asti ny atraye mahiṣvantaṁ yuyotam | yo vāṁ omānaṁ dadhate priyaḥ san ||
english: Truly wondrous is your gift; keep the buffalo-drinker away from Atri — he who being dear to you places his trust in your protection.

sanskrit: uta tyad vāṁ jurate aśvinā bhūc cyavānāya pratītyaṁ havirde | adhi yad varpa itaūti dhatthaḥ ||
english: And that, O Aśvins, which was given to Cyavāna as an oblation-gift approached you for protection — because you bestow special form and aid upon him.

sanskrit: uta tyam bhujyum aśvinā sakhāyo madhye jahur durevāsaḥ samudre | nir īm parṣad arāvā yo yuvākuḥ ||
english: And Bhujyu whom his companions, hard to live with, had abandoned in the midst of the sea — carry him out, O Aśvins, the one who is without a helper but longs for you.

sanskrit: vṛkāya cij jasamānāya śaktam uta śrutaṁ śayave hūyamānā | yāv aghnyām apinvatam apo na staryaṁ cic chakty aśvinā śacībhiḥ ||
english: Grant help even to the wolf that is in distress, and hear when Śaya calls upon you — you two who filled the barren cow with milk like water for a dry one with your powers, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: eṣa sya kārur jarate sūktair agre budhāna uṣasāṁ sumanmā | iṣā taṁ vardhad aghnyā payobhir yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: This singer wakes and praises with well-spoken hymns in the van of the Dawns, of good intention. May the inviolable cow enrich him with her milk; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ ratho rodasī badbadhāno hiraṇyayo vṛṣabhir yātv aśvaiḥ | ghṛtavartaniḥ pavibhī rucāna iṣāṁ voḻhā nṛpatir vājinīvān ||
english: Let your chariot come to us, O Aśvins — golden, filling the two worlds, drawn by bulls and horses; with its track of ghee, flashing with its wheel-rims, the lord of men who bears nourishment and wins prizes.

sanskrit: sa papratāno abhi pañca bhūmā trivandhuḥ manasā yātu yuktaḥ | viśo yena gacchatho devayantīḥ kutrā cid yāmam aśvinā dadhānā ||
english: Spreading itself across the five regions, triple-thonged, moving with purpose, let it come harnessed; with which you two visit god-seeking peoples wherever you choose to direct your course, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: svaśvā yaśasā yātam arvāg dasrā nidhim madhumantam pibāthaḥ | vi vāṁ ratho vadhvā yādamāno 'ntān divo bādhate vartanibhyām ||
english: Come hither with your glorious fair horses, O wonder-workers; drink the honey-sweet treasure. Your chariot, moving with the wife beside it, drives back the ends of heaven with its wheel-tracks.

sanskrit: yuvoḥ śriyam pari yoṣāvṛṇīta sūro duhitā paritakmyāyām | yad devayantam avathaḥ śacībhiḥ pari ghraṁsam omanā vāṁ vayo gāt ||
english: The Sun's daughter has chosen the glory of you two in the race; when you have aided the god-seeking one with your powers, your strength goes around the heat of the sun with your protection.

sanskrit: yo ha sya vāṁ rathirā vasta usrā ratho yujānaḥ pariyāti vartiḥ | tena naḥ śaṁ yor uṣaso vyuṣṭau ny aśvinā vahataṁ yajñe asmin ||
english: He who dresses at dawn as your charioteer — that chariot, as it is yoked, circles its track. With that, O Aśvins, at the shining forth of the Dawn for our wellbeing and ease, convey us to this sacrifice.

sanskrit: narā gaureva vidyutaṁ tṛṣāṇāsmākam adya savanoṣa yātam | purutrā hi vāṁ matibhir havante mā vāṁ anye ni yaman devayantaḥ ||
english: O two lords, thirsting like a buffalo-cow for lightning, come today to our pressing; for in many places men call upon you with their thoughts — may no other god-seekers constrain you away from us.

sanskrit: yuvam bhujyum avaviddhaṁ samudra ud ūhathuḥ arṇaso asridhānaiḥ | patratribhir aśramair avyathibhir daṁsanābhir aśvinā pārayantā ||
english: You two lifted Bhujyu who had fallen into the sea, carrying him up from the flood with your boats that do not tire, that do not swerve, that do not sink — with your wondrous craft, O Aśvins, bearing him across.

sanskrit: nū me havam ā śṛṇutaṁ yuvānā yāsiṣṭaṁ vartir aśvināv irāvat | dhattaṁ ratnāni jarataṁ ca sūrīn yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Now hear my call, O two young ones; come, O Aśvins, on a path that brings refreshment. Bestow treasures and let the patrons grow old in honor; guard us ever with blessings.

sanskrit: ā viśvavārāśvinā gataṁ naḥ pra tat sthānam avāci vāṁ pṛthivyām | aśvo na vājī śunapṛṣṭho asthād ā yat sedathur dhruvase na yonim ||
english: Come to us, O Aśvins of universal bounty; that place has been proclaimed for you on the earth. Like a prize-winning horse with the dog on its back standing ready — when you two sit down as in a fixed station.

sanskrit: siṣakti sā vāṁ sumatiś caniṣṭhātāpi gharmo manuṣo duroṇe | yo vāṁ samudrān saritas piparty etagvā cin na suyujā yujānaḥ ||
english: That goodwill most dear to you two follows close; the hot oblation is shared in the house of the mortal; he who fills the rivers to the seas for you, harnessing as if with well-yoked steeds — even the swift one.

sanskrit: yāni sthānāny aśvinā dadhāthe divo yahvīṣv oṣadhīṣu vikṣu | ni parvatasya mūrdhani sadanteṣaṁ janāya dāśuṣe vahantā ||
english: The stations which you two Aśvins have established — on the great rivers of heaven, among the plants, among the peoples — sitting on the peak of the mountain, carry refreshment to the worshipping mortal.

sanskrit: caniṣṭaṁ devā oṣadhīṣv apsu yad yogyā aśnaVaithe ṛṣīṇām | purūṇi ratnā dadhatau ny asme anu pūrvāṇi cakhyathur yugāni ||
english: The gods have delighted in the plants and waters — what the sages attain to when fit for yoking — you two have laid many treasures down for us, looking after the former ages in order.

sanskrit: śuśruvāṁsā cid aśvinā purūṇy abhi brahmāṇi cakṣāthe ṛṣīṇām | prati pra yātaṁ varam ā janāyāsme vām astu sumatiś caniṣṭhā ||
english: Even though you have heard many a prayer of the sages, O Aśvins, you look upon them; come and bring the best to the people; may the goodwill most dear to you be ours.

sanskrit: yo vāṁ yajño nāsatyā haviṣmān kṛtabrahmā samaryo bhavāti | upa pra yātaṁ varam ā vasiṣṭham imā brahmāṇy ṛcyante yuvabhyām ||
english: Whichever sacrifice to you, O Nāsatyā, has oblations, with prayers composed and fit for the assembly — come near and bring the best to Vasiṣṭha; these prayers are sung for you two.

sanskrit: iyam manīṣā iyam aśvinā gīr imāṁ suvṛktiṁ vṛṣaṇā juṣethām | imā brahmāṇi yuvayūny agman yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: This meditation, this song, O Aśvins — delight in this eloquent praise, O mighty bulls; these prayers have come longing for you two; guard us ever with blessings.
